summary.intent: Determine what uncommitted changes were in the wisp-plugins repo, clean up, and commit them and open a PR for the Smith implementation-context integration, repo rename updates, and Entire hook changes.
summary.outcome: Removed generated __pycache__ dirs, fixed a stale Codex hook entry, verified with `just check` (49 tests passing), and after user confirmation made three commits onto a fresh branch from origin/main and proceeded to open the PR. Final PR creation result was not shown in the transcript.

repo: Repo uses `just check` as the readiness gate: runs 49 tests, version checks, generated marketplace check, and Mermaid validation.
Changes are organized into plugin harness directories (harnesses/codex, dist/codex) with generated Codex files that must stay in sync with plugin sources.
Entire is intended to automatically push checkpoints and sessions; those settings in .entire/settings.json are deliberate, not accidental.
Courier commit/PR workflows require explicit user confirmation of exact commit messages, scope, and PR draft before committing or publishing.
Branch's earlier PR #15 was already merged, so new work needed a fresh branch from current origin/main to preserve newer README and hero images.
Commit convention is conventional commits with scopes, e.g. feat(smith), chore(repo), chore(entire).

code.finding: A Codex PreToolUse Agent entry still invoked `entire hooks claude-code pre-task`; the installed Entire CLI has no `codex pre-task` handler, so the entry was removed since Codex SubagentStart (`codex subagent-start`) already covers that event.
Enables automatic checkpoint and session pushes; intentional per user.

workflow: Check for overlap between staged and unstaged changes (a file like Smith's README can appear in both) before grouping commits.
Split mixed working-tree changes into separate topical commits (feature, rename, hooks config) rather than one large commit.
Verify generated artifacts (e.g. __pycache__) are untracked and delete before committing.
Confirm the remote/merge state of the branch before opening a PR, since a prior PR may already be merged.

friction: `gh` could not reach GitHub at first, delaying the remote step.
User had to correct the assistant twice that Entire checkpoint/session pushes are intentional, after the assistant flagged them as needing review.
Branch's earlier PR was already merged, requiring re-basing the work onto a fresh branch from origin/main.
open_items: Confirm the PR in orin-dx/wisp-plugins was actually created successfully; its URL/result was not shown.
Local branch was one commit ahead of remote (the implementation-context schema commit), which is carried onto the new branch.
